00-one-shot.py: VERIFIED against plate map pcr-02. 24 of 24 wells hold what the plate map
  says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3). Reading of the request: 24
    reactions.

Labware for the technique (PCR setup): 1 finding.
1. NOTE LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: master mix is declared in a reservoir channel, not a tube
   line 48:  reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix, volume=500)   # µL
   Line 48 declares 500 ul of master mix in channel A1 of NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL (slot
     4, load name nest_12_reservoir_15ml). The request (PCR setup) puts its reagents in
     tubes, or at a temperature, and a reservoir channel is neither: 500 ul spread over the
     channel is 1.7 mm deep, open to the air and at room temperature, so it warms and
     evaporates while the run goes on, and the tip may not reach it.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Put master mix in a tube on the block (a tube rack, or a temperature module with a
     tube block), not in a reservoir channel.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1
   [bb7daa1d701c]

00-one-shot.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 1 warning, 2 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 23 stocks
   line 75:  p20.aspirate(2, src)
   At line 75 the tip went into sample 5 (tube A2 in slot 2), sample 9 (tube A3 in slot 2),
   sample 13 (tube A4 in slot 2), sample 17 (tube A5 in slot 2) and 19 more while it still
   carried sample 1 (tube A1 in slot 2), sample 5 (tube A2 in slot 2), sample 9 (tube A3 in
   slot 2), sample 13 (tube A4 in slot 2) and 21 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   23 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 23 other wells: wells A2, A3, B1, B2, B3,
   C1, C2, C3 and 15 more in slot 3.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 15 more in slot 2.
   Also reached 23 other wells: wells A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2, C3 and 15 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 75 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [f6276c72977e]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (well A2 in slot 4)
   line 67:  p20.aspirate(10.5, reservoir["A2"])
   At line 67 the tip went into water (well A2 in slot 4) while it still carried master mix
   (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that
   were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in
   the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: well A2 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 67 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [ea8558f14e48]

3. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 24 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 60:  p20.dispense(12.5, dest)
   At line 60 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 3), and 24 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2
   and 16 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 12.5 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [91af2cfdda84]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 24 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 20 more went in (8% of the well)
   line 76:  p20.dispense(2, dest)
   At line 76 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 20 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 3, which already held master mix and
   water (this line did it 24 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the
   well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small
   well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one
   will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 3 after line 76:
   `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [e686415b1e3d]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
